title: ELVTR sprite generation request
description: The contract between the art director's prose spec and the PixelLab generation pipeline. One file per subject in docs/data/art/requests/<id>.json. Authored by pixel-art-director; consumed by Scripts/art/pixelpipe.py and the /sprite skill. Structural rules live here; canon rules (retired hexes, palette existence, spec-file resolution) are enforced by pixelpipe.py validate, which JSON Schema cannot express.
comment_composite: Two shapes of request exist. A SUBJECT request (no 'composite' key) describes one thing to generate and requires the full prompt/pixellab/anchor/canon/budget set. A COMPOSITE request generates nothing — it packs frames other requests already produced into one shared texture — so those blocks are meaningless for it and are not required. The conditional below is why the root 'required' list is expressed as if/then rather than a flat array.

composite.description: Marks this as a composite request: one texture assembled from SEVERAL subjects. Added 2026-07-25 because the swarm atlas (T_Swarm_2bit) holds both teams in one sheet — the Niagara emitter has a single sprite renderer with a single material, so splitting it into one texture per subject would need a renderer change and would lose the single-index SubUV decode in SwarmSheet::CellForBits. Nothing here is generated; frame_map keys become '<prefix>:<direction>.<state>'.

sources.description: Where each group of cells comes from. Every source needs a prefix and exactly one of 'request' or 'frames'.

prefix.description: Namespace for this source's frame keys in frame_map, e.g. 'retinue' -> 'retinue:south.walk1'.

request.description: id of a pipeline-managed subject request whose quantized frames to draw from. Its own quantize stage must have run.

frames.description: UNMANAGED source: an explicit frame-key -> repo-relative PNG map, for placeholder art that did not come through the pipeline. Recorded in the manifest as provenance 'placeholder' and flagged by report, so a sheet can ship with a stand-in without the manifest claiming it was generated here.

quantize.description: Run the canonical palette snap on this source's frames at pack time. Managed sources are already quantized so this is a cheap no-op; unmanaged ones usually need it.

note.description: Why this source is shaped the way it is — especially why an unmanaged source is still a placeholder.

id.description: Stable kebab-case slug. Names the render folder (RawArt/Renders/<id>/) and must never change once generations have been spent against it — the manifest is keyed on it.

revision.description: Bump on ANY change to prompt or pixellab params. Each revision gets its own r<n>/ folder so old generations are never overwritten (retention rule).

kind.description: Drives defaults and validation. 'ui' is the only kind exempt from the 48px cell rule and from 2x2 dither enforcement.

faction.description: Free-form, and normally 'none'. Current canon (docs/narrative/FLAME-FOUNDATION.md §5) deliberately names NO factions — the 2026-07-22 reset discarded the Still Legion, the Quiet and the Unwitnessed, and replacements are held back until the prototype answers what the world needs to contain. Naming one here is a canon proposal, not a lookup.

brief.description: Optional path to the originating brief, relative to this file's directory. This file lives in docs/data/art/requests/, so docs/briefs/ is THREE levels up: ../../../briefs/brief-00N-slug.md

spec.description: REQUIRED path to the prose spec this request implements, relative to this file's directory. This file lives in docs/data/art/requests/, so docs/art/ is THREE levels up: ../../../art/vanguard.md. Validated to exist. Every canon field below must be traceable to a line in it.

canon.description: The art-direction constraints the pipeline enforces mechanically. Not suggestions to the model — checks run against the output.

palette.description: Key into docs/data/art/palette.json 'palettes'. Anything other than demichrome-4 requires an explicit owner exception.

value_dominance.description: Which of the four values should dominate the sprite. Feeds the disjointness audit in docs/art/npc-silhouette-brief.md — with hue gone, value dominance is one of only three channels separating factions. The QC report flags a sprite whose actual histogram contradicts this.

pale_usage.description: How this subject is allowed to spend the single bright value. 'none' means the QC report flags ANY pale pixel — that is how the Still Legion's no-bright rule is enforced. Non-'none' values should match the subject's shape-carrier in palette.json.

silhouette.description: The shape language, in words, from the spec (e.g. 'lines and geometry', 'amorphous, non-geometric').

reads_as.description: The one-line 'reads as' statement, copied verbatim from the prose spec. Composed into the prompt.

moving.description: True for anything animated or moving in-game => 2x2 minimum dither block is enforced by the quantizer. False only for static UI and portraits, where 1px halftone is legal.

light_shift_variant.description: Emit a second sheet with every value shifted one step brighter, for the Lampbearer's lamp radius. Uses palette.json light_shift.map — no new hexes, no regeneration.

prompt.description: Prompt INPUTS, not the final string. pixelpipe.py prompt composes the string deterministically from these plus canon plus palette.json. Never hand-type a description at call time — deterministic composition is what substitutes for PixelLab's missing seed.

description.description: Appearance only. No palette hexes (the composer adds those), no camera/view language (that is a pixellab param), no environment.

must_include.description: Silhouette carriers that must survive to the final sprite. Composed into the prompt AND printed on the stage-D review checklist so the human gate knows what to look for.

must_avoid.description: Composed as negative guidance. The composer always appends the house set (saturated colour, gradients, anti-aliasing) — list only subject-specific additions here.

style_mode.description: Which house style clause the composer appends. 'flat' is the locked look (aesthetic-direction.md Direction A): adds 'flat unlit pixel art, hard pixel edges, dither for any intermediate tone' and forbids gradients/anti-aliasing/soft shading. 'depth' is a RENDER-TREATMENT EXPERIMENT ONLY: it drops the flat clause and lifts those three negatives so a shading param above 'flat shading' is not fighting its own prompt. It does NOT lift the palette — output is still quantized to the 4-value ramp. No shipping asset may use 'depth' without an explicit owner exception.

pixellab.description: Literal create_character arguments. Mirrors the MCP tool schema — keep in sync if PixelLab changes it. Note there is NO seed field: create_character does not accept one.

mode.description: Use 'standard' for a text-to-sprite anchor: it is the ONLY mode that honours shading, proportions and text_guidance_scale, and it costs 1 generation instead of 2. v3 silently ignores all three (plus n_directions) -- its strength is the rotation pass, where style comes from reference_image_base64 rather than from params. Measured on hero-vanguard r1: a v3 anchor discarded 'chibi' and 'flat shading' and failed the spec on five counts.

n_directions.description: Ignored by pro and v3 (always 8). Kept for standard-mode anchors.

shading.description: Ignored by v3 and pro. Kept because a standard-mode anchor honours it as soft guidance.

proportions.description: Serialized to a JSON string at call time. The chibi ruling of 2026-07-11 stands for combat-scale heroes, retinue and Legion; Unwitnessed titans are non-chibi.

text_guidance_scale.description: Ignored by v3. Raise on a standard-mode anchor to push harder toward the description.

template.description: Required when body_type is quadruped: bear, cat, dog, horse, lion.

anchor.description: How style consistency is achieved. PixelLab enforces no palette and offers no seed, so the anchor IS the style contract: one quantized frame fed back via v3 reference_image_base64 propagates our exact ramp to every rotation and animation frame.

strategy.description: authored: render the prose spec's own ASCII pixel map as the anchor via 'pixelpipe.py authored' -- zero generations, on-palette by construction, and it cannot come back missing the subject's defining prop (the failure that killed hero-vanguard r2). Prefer this whenever the spec has a silhouette guide. quantized-self: generate an anchor from text, quantize it, feed it back as the v3 reference. text-only: no reference image at all, lowest fidelity, use only to explore. shared-anchor: reuse another request's approved anchor so a group shares one style source.

source_direction.description: Which rotation becomes the anchor. v3 expects a south-facing sprite; changing this is unusual.

shared_anchor_id.description: Required when strategy is shared-anchor: the id of the request whose approved anchor to reuse.

approved.description: Set true by a human at the stage-D gate. The pipeline refuses to run the rotation pass until this is true — everything downstream inherits the anchor, so an unapproved anchor wastes the whole batch.

template_animation_id.description: Required when mode is template. Cheapest route at 1 generation/direction. Common: walk, walking-4-frames, running-4-frames, breathing-idle.

action_description.description: Required when mode is v3 or pro. Movement/pose only — no environment.

frame_count.description: Honoured only in v3 mode; must be even. Template mode uses the template's count; pro mode fixes it by size.

directions.description: Omit to animate all character directions in template mode. v3 defaults to south only.

portrait.description: Optional bust portrait via create_portrait_character(direction=character_to_portrait). There is no text-to-portrait tool — a portrait is always derived from a finished sprite.

result_size.description: 128 and 160 render at 2K for extra detail and cost 25 generations; 16-64 cost 20.

cell.description: Sprite cell size in px. Locked to 48 for every kind except ui (owner decision, 2026-07-25). pixelpipe.py validate enforces this — the schema cannot express the conditional.

grid.description: [columns, rows]. Both must be powers of two — the Niagara SubUV requirement from ELVTR/SETUP-EDITOR.md. The texture itself need not be power-of-two (4x4 x 48 = 192x192 is fine).

frame_map.description: Cell index (as a string) -> frame key of the form <direction>.<state>, e.g. "0": "south.idle", "1": "south.walk1". Cells are numbered left-to-right, top-to-bottom. Unlisted cells are left transparent. Keys must resolve to frames the pipeline actually produced — validated at pack time, not schema time.

texture.description: UE texture asset name. T_ prefix per the repo's naming convention.

content_path.description: Destination package path for the import step, e.g. /Game/Sprites/Units.

sheet_srgb.description: sRGB on for colour sheets; false for mask-only textures, per docs/ui/UI-PROTOTYPE-PLAN.md.

max_generations.description: Hard ceiling for this request across all revisions of a single run. The skill checks get_balance first and refuses to exceed this. Reference costs: v3 anchor at 48px = 2, v3 rotation = 2, template animation = 1/direction, portrait = 20-25, pro = 20-40/direction.
